title: introduce-delimsplice-anchor-and-order-hedge-for-sse
author: Priya Anand
description:
Context: intermittent customer incidents in the OpenAI-compat streaming layer where partial JSON objects and interleaved event delimiters caused consumer-side JSON parse errors and fncall ordering anomalies. Root causes identified: (1) stream fragments arriving out-of-order during multi-worker flushes, (2) delimiter bytes being coalesced or split across chunk boundaries by the socket layer, and (3) fncall sentinel emission not always honoring the logical ordinal when backpressure and batching reorder fragments. This PR introduces a two-part runtime mitigation: a 'delimsplice anchor' that inserts an ephemeral, stateless anchor token to mark safe reassembly boundaries, and an 'order hedge' that maintains per-session ordinal windows to preserve fncall ordering until the anchor is validated.
Design summary:
- Delimsplice anchor: a short, opaque ASCII-safe marker emitted by the server only when a fragment crosses a batch boundary. The marker is dropped from final payloads but used transiently by the reassembler to align JSON spans across chunks. It is enabled behind a feature flag (stream_delimsplice_anchor) and emits only when socket-level coalescing is detected.
- Order hedge: a lightweight ordinal lease that tags fncall sentinel events with a small epoch number and checksum; consumers can use it to reject out-of-ordinals until a matching anchor confirms continuity. The hedge is conservative (small numeric window) to avoid stalling low-latency paths.
Implementation notes:
- Changes are limited to the openai-compat SSE encoder, the stream reassembly state machine, and the fncall sentinel emission path.
- The anchor payload is designed to avoid producing valid JSON tokens (prefix "~|#D" anchor). It is stripped during final serializing pass so it is invisible to normal API outputs.
- We add a reassembly step that recognizes anchors, aligns fragments, validates UTF-8 boundaries, and then drains the anchor before handing the token stream to existing JSON parsers.
- Feature flag gating and telemetry hooks are included.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled.
Rollout plan: 1) ship behind feature flag on canary hosts, 2) observe telemetry (partial-json-rescue, anchor-match-rate, ordered-fncall-drop-rate) for 48 hours, 3) enable for 10% of traffic, 4) progressive rollout to 100% if no regressions.
Security/privacy: anchors contain no user data and are ephemeral; no new surface for secrets.
Related issues/links: Linear ENG-3421, ENG-3480, docs: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421, internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sse-partial-json.
Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for anchor insertion and removal
- [x] Integration test exercising coalesced chunks from netcat-level simulation
- [x] E2E smoke against OpenAI-compat examples
- [x] Telemetry hooks and dashboard panels
- [x] Feature flag behind org-level gating
- [x] Docs note in openai-compat streaming guide

ci_status: pass (unit, integration), flaky on one e2e; reran and green
review_conversation: Ethan Cole: Found a potential race where an anchor could be dropped if the reassembly window exits before the trailing fragment arrives. Suggest keeping a short linger timer per-session (100ms) before expiring an anchor.
Priya Anand: Added a 100ms linger with adaptive backoff based on observed RTT; updated tests to cover linger expiry and added telemetry for linger-triggered rescues.
María López: Can we guarantee the anchor token will never collide with user content? The prefix helps but we should also assert removal at final serialization.
Priya Anand: Agreed; serialization step now asserts anchor-free output and we added a fuzz test to detect escrowed tokens.
Samir Patel: Perf concern: extra reassembly step increases CPU for high-rt workload. Measured overhead ~0.8% p99 CPU on canary. OK for rollout behind flag.
Ethan Cole: Approving after seeing integration test results and telemetry wiring.
ci_details: CI run 2026-02-18: unit tests passed; integration target flaky due to netcat simulation timing; fixed test harness and reran 2026-02-19 with green. E2E smoke executed on canary cluster during staged rollout and reported no regressions.
release_notes: Improves resilience of SSE streaming reassembly by adding an anchor token and ordering hedge to recover partial JSON and preserve fncall ordering under coalesced/chunked streams. Disabled by default; rollout controlled via feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag stream_delimsplice_anchor on canary hosts by setting feature_flags.stream_delimsplice_anchor=true in org config. Watch telemetry: partial-json-rescue, anchor-match-rate, ordered-fncall-drop-rate. If anchor-match-rate is low and parse errors increase, roll back the flag immediately.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover anchor insertion/removal, reassembly alignment, and ordinal hedging. Integration netcat simulation reproduces socket coalescing scenarios. Canary E2E smoke validated against openai-compat clients (python/ts). Performance impact measured at ~0.8% CPU at p99 on canary under synthetic coalescing load.
